turns.t: Hello doctor. I am having this redness on my face only, since two years now. It is not going, and I am feeling very conscious.
Okay, Mrs. Raghunathan. Sit down. Show me where it is worst, and tell me what you notice.
Here, on both cheeks and the nose. It is... how to say, it is red like I am blushing always. And sometimes on the forehead also.
Red cheeks and nose, since two years. Does the redness stay all day, or does it come in waves?
Waves, mostly. It becomes too much when I drink hot tea or when I eat spicy food. Then my face is... flushing, flushing like a heater.
So hot drinks and spicy food set off the flushing. Anything else that triggers it?
Sun, also. And in the kitchen, when I am standing near the stove.
Sun and heat. Is there any pain with it, or a burning feeling?
Burning, yes. Like a stinging, especially after washing my face with soap.
Okay. Are there any spots, bumps, or pimples along with the redness?
Small bumps, yes, a few. Like pimples, but no head on them. They come and go.
Any itching, joint pains or fevers with this?
No, no itching. No joint pains, no fever. Nothing like that.
Good. What about your eyes? Any dryness, redness or blurred vision?
No, eyes are fine, doctor. Nothing in the eyes.
Alright. Now, what medicines are you using right now, for the face or anything else?
For the face, I am using the metronidazole gel, twice a day. And at night the azelaic acid cream.
Metronidazole gel twice a day, azelaic acid at night. Any tablets?
Yes, metformin, 500 mg, morning and night. And levothyroxine, 50 micrograms, every morning on empty stomach.
Metformin and levothyroxine. And for what conditions are those?
Type 2 diabetes, since some years. And thyroid, underactive thyroid, I have.
Type 2 diabetes and an underactive thyroid. Fine. Do you have any allergies to medicines or creams?
No, no allergies. I am using everything without problem, only this redness is not going.
Good. Any operations in the past?
Appendix I got removed when I was twelve years old. And the gallbladder, in 2015.
Appendix at twelve, gallbladder in 2015. Does anyone in your family have skin problems like this?
My mother had rosacea. Same red face. She also never went to doctor, she only used home remedies.
That's useful. Now a few questions about your lifestyle. Do you smoke?
Never. I never smoked, not even once.
And alcohol?
Occasionally only, a glass of wine on weekends. That is all.
What work do you do?
I am a school teacher. Primary class, so playground duty in the sun also.
Do you exercise at all?
I walk every morning, forty minutes. In the sun, sir, at seven o'clock only. Is it bad?
Early enough to be mild. Let me take your readings first. Blood pressure is 126 over 80.
Pulse is 76, temperature 36.8 degrees, oxygen saturation 98 percent. Your weight is 72 kilograms.
Everything normal?
All normal. Now let me look at your face under the light. Please face me, and keep your eyes closed.
There is redness across both cheeks and the nose, with a few small red bumps.
I don't see any blackheads, so this is most likely rosacea, rather than acne.
Rosacea, like my mother. Will it go away completely?
It's long-term, but it can be controlled well. The first step is protecting the skin. Use a sunscreen every morning, SPF 30 at least, and a gentle cleanser instead of soap.
Even in the kitchen, near the stove? I cannot avoid that.
Do what you can. Keep your face back from the steam, and let the tea cool first.
I will try. Should I stop the gel and cream, then?
No, continue both as you are. I'd like to order liver function tests, since you're on metformin and thyroid medicine and we may adjust treatment later.
Fine. I had my blood sugar test done last month, only. Should I bring that report?
Yes, please bring it. I'd also like to book a patch test, to see whether any cream or cosmetic is aggravating your skin, small patches on the back for two days.
One more thing. If the redness doesn't settle with all this, we might consider a small skin biopsy to be sure of the diagnosis.
Biopsy? That is cutting the skin? I am afraid.
It's only a tiny sample under local anaesthetic, and only if we need it. Not now. Let's see how you respond first.
Okay. When should I come again?
Come back in six weeks, with the test results ready.
Six weeks. Thank you, doctor. I was very worried, I thought it is something serious.
It's not dangerous. Keep a diary of what triggers the flushing, that will help us a lot. Take care.
